answer: Foot pushes the pedal, the pedal pushes a piston, the piston pushes the brake fluid, pressure goes down the brake line to the caliper, the caliper's pistons then squeeze the pads onto the disc at the wheel.
Because fluid can't be squeezed (it can't be compressed), so the pressure travels along.
A spinning metal disc (labelled DISC, the wheel).

Two pads, one on each side, side by side with the disc between them under the caliper. The picture shows two pads placed apart; the words say two pads squeeze against the disc. Which sides of the disc is not clearly shown.
It is turned into heat by friction; the disc turns hot and can glow after a hard stop.
